rejected.title: Overweight and obesity
card: Overweight and obesity mean having more body fat than is healthy. Body mass index (BMI) compares weight with height. For adults, 25 to under 30 is overweight and 30 or more is obese.
Excess body weight raises the risk of type 2 diabetes, heart disease and some cancers. A higher risk does not mean a person will get these conditions.

Excess fat can make the body respond less to insulin, the hormone that moves sugar out of the blood and into cells, so sugar builds up in the blood. Type 1 diabetes is different: the immune system destroys the cells that make insulin.

rejected.remember: Excess weight makes type 2 diabetes, heart disease and some cancers more likely, not certain.

a.q: How can excess body fat raise the risk of type 2 diabetes?
opts: It can make the body respond less to insulin
It destroys the cells that make insulin
It lowers the level of sugar in the blood
It makes cells take in sugar too quickly
a.why: Excess fat can make the body respond less to insulin, so sugar is not moved into cells and builds up in the blood. The immune system destroying insulin-making cells describes type 1 diabetes, which is not caused by body weight.
a.clue: Type 2 and type 1 diabetes go wrong in different ways.

b.q: Dev is an adult with a BMI of 31. Which statement about his health is most accurate?
opts: He is in the obese range, so heart disease is more likely
He is in the overweight range, so he will get heart disease
He is in the obese range, so he will get type 2 diabetes
He is in the overweight range, so cancer is more likely
b.why: A BMI of 30 or more is classed as obese, and excess weight raises the risk of heart disease. The options saying he will get heart disease or type 2 diabetes treat a raised risk as a certainty. The options placing him in the overweight range are wrong, as that range ends below 30.
b.clue: Check which range 31 falls in, then check whether a condition is said to be certain.

draft.title: Overweight and obesity
card: Overweight and obesity mean having more body fat than is healthy. Health workers often screen for them using body mass index (BMI), which compares weight with height.
For adults, a BMI of 25 to under 30 is classed as overweight. A BMI of 30 or more is classed as obese.
Excess body weight raises the risk of type 2 diabetes, heart disease and some cancers. It does not mean a person will get these conditions.
Because these conditions are common, excess body weight adds to Australia's burden of disease, which is the total harm that illness and early death cause.
draft.remember: Excess body weight raises the risk of several major conditions, so it adds to the burden of disease.

a.q: Which of these is a health risk linked to excess body weight?
opts: Type 2 diabetes
Scurvy
Measles
Hearing loss from noise
a.why: Excess body weight raises the risk of type 2 diabetes, along with heart disease and some cancers. Scurvy comes from too little vitamin C, measles is an infection and noise damage is an injury, so none of them is linked to body weight in this way.
a.clue: Think of a long-term condition that affects how the body handles sugar.

b.q: Dev is an adult with a BMI of 31. Which statement about his health is most accurate?
opts: He is in the obese range, so his heart disease risk is higher
He is in the overweight range, so he will get heart disease
He is in the obese range, so he will get type 2 diabetes
He is in the overweight range, so his cancer risk is higher
b.why: A BMI of 30 or more is classed as obese, and excess body weight raises the risk of heart disease. The second and third options wrongly say he will get a condition, but the card says only that risk rises. The fourth names the wrong range.
b.clue: Check which range 31 falls in, and watch for wording that says a condition is certain.
